correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and first small lake-like reach
correspondence.finding: The actual short headward opening is absent from the generalized linework. The following southward small waterbody is depicted without a name, but its connection through the masked upper corridor cannot be established. A nearby northern or western river label is not assigned to it.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper southwest bend, southeast return and approach toward Durocher
correspondence.finding: The station074902 data box physically covers the selected upper route and its intermediate waterbody connections. The supplied model route cannot reveal hidden source linework, and visible reaches above and below the box do not prove the intervening through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Visible Durocher lake passage and southeast connection
correspondence.finding: Below the data box, the selected path follows the depicted lake corridor carrying the Lac Durocher label, continues southeast, and turns eastward toward the northern Musquaro approach. The obscured upstream approach remains a separate material gap; the lake name is not extended to every feeder or connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern narrowing and approach into Musquaro
correspondence.finding: The source depicts the connected southward neck and widening approach into the long central lake complex, separate from the neighboring eastern Goyelle drainage. This confirms ordinary geographic correspondence without assigning a river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lac Musquaro passage and southern lake-complex exit
correspondence.finding: The selected long southward route traverses the extensive irregular waterbody labeled Lac Musquaro, including its narrowing, broadening and southern connections. The source shows the passage as connected at regional scale. Exact internal lake-versus-river boundaries and names of individual bays or narrows are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest return, broadened lower waters and southeast bend
correspondence.finding: The selected southwest-trending river/waterbody corridor and subsequent southeast bend follow the original hydrographic linework. The sheet prints Lac du Grand Priant across this lower lake setting. The label is retained as mapped context, without assigning that name to every selected reach or resolving its exact lake-name extent. The eastern Washicoutai corridor remains distinct.

correspondence.component_scope: Join between both selected mainstem fragments and lower coastal course
correspondence.finding: The final southeast bend of the first fragment continues into the eastward and southeastward course of the second on the original map. This is a source-observed geographic continuation at regional scale, not merely acceptance of the model fragment join.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal approach and receiving coast
correspondence.finding: The final southward selected segment follows the mapped lower watercourse to the depicted Gulf of St.Lawrence coast. The source supports this ordinary coastal outlet setting. Exact bank, tidal boundary, named bay and open-sea mouth placement are not certified and are not imposed as extra completion requirements.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and first connection to the mapped northern watercourse
correspondence.finding: The short selected east-west opening is not continuously depicted as a separate connection to the north-south headwater line on the generalized CEHQ original. The later park-study map begins well south of this opening. Basin membership and the adjacent mapped headwater waterbody do not establish this chosen initial connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern lake-and-river chain and approach to the park-study extent
correspondence.finding: South of the unresolved opening, the selected westward bend, southeastward descent, broadened waters and intervening southward links correspond to the continuous eastern chain on the CEHQ original. The western Schmon route is distinct. The nearby Petit lac du Nord label is not assigned to a selected waterbody because its placement alone is insufficient. No upstream river name is extended from a downstream label.

correspondence.component_scope: Lac Ulysse-Morin approach, lake passage and outgoing Gravel corridor
correspondence.finding: Carte1 places Lac Ulysse-Morin on the selected northern approach to the Gravel valley. Its longitudinal lake passage and outgoing river are visible, consistent with the broader CEHQ chain. The lake keeps its own identity; the adjoining river reaches are not all renamed as the lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Rivière Gravel, tributary join and entry to northern Lac Walker
correspondence.finding: The selected southwest-trending and then southward meandering valley follows the labeled Gravel corridor on Carte1 to the northern end of Lac Walker. The report describes the Petite rivière Gravel confluence and subsequent southwestward reach. Its separate western Schmon valley also enters Walker; that western route is not substituted for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Longitudinal Lac Walker passage and southern lake outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected north-to-south lake passage follows the elongated Walker waterbody and reaches its mapped southern outlet. Carte1 distinguishes neighboring Lac Pasteur to the east and Lac Quatre Lieues to the southwest. Neither adjoining lake is treated as a selected through-passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Rivière aux Rochers below Walker and eastward course to the fragment join
correspondence.finding: The Walker outlet leads south along the separately labeled Rivière aux Rochers, then turns east. Carte1 and the report’s MacDonald discussion distinguish the adjoining Quatre Lieues/MacDonald connection. The eastward selected course reaches the source-depicted bend at the FID boundary; the supplied fragments are not treated as separate unrelated rivers.

correspondence.component_scope: Joined lower Rivière aux Rochers and Port-Cartier coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The two-fragment join lies on the continuous mapped receiving corridor. The selected lower fragment turns south and east through the Port-Cartier approach and reaches the river’s coastal outlet. Carte1 depicts the lower watercourse, its coastal branches and connection to the Golfe du Saint-Laurent; CEHQ independently shows the coast-reaching river. This establishes the ordinary terminal setting without assigning an exact shoreline, bank, tidal boundary or current branch-operation condition.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and local feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the upper Woolfe Fork valley beside a short eastern feeder. Original cartography depicts this feeder joining the continuously mapped Woolfe Fork channel. The selected opening is not identified as the ultimate natural source or a formal named-source point.

correspondence.component_scope: Woolfe Fork northward corridor
correspondence.finding: Repeated Woolfe Fork labels follow the connected northward channel. The eastern and western side feeders are visibly connected to that channel; none is given the scalar name of the receiving river. The selected path is coarse and locally cuts small valley bends.

correspondence.component_scope: Woolfe Fork–Ipewik River junction
correspondence.finding: The source shows Woolfe Fork meeting the separately labelled Ipewik River, which approaches from the east, then the combined channel continues north and northwest. This mapped confluence, rather than proximity of labels or model connectivity, supports the name transition.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Ipewik bends and Windy Lake side-drainage setting
correspondence.finding: The original map shows a continuous meandering Ipewik River around the upper northern bends and onward to the western valley. The pinned selection makes pronounced cutoffs north of several actual mapped bends. Correspondence is to this continuous receiving-river corridor, not to an asserted separate waterway along each cutoff. Windy Lake lies north of the main river on a side drainage; the selected route does not require a through-lake passage. Its name is not extended to the river.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Ipewik corridor and Niilik River joining setting
correspondence.finding: Repeated Ipewik River labels and the continuous mapped westward channel cover the middle bends and intervening side-tributary mouths. Niilik River is separately labelled on the northern incoming waterway, and its confluence with Ipewik is visible. The selected route approaches from the east along Ipewik and proceeds southwest after the junction; Niilik is a tributary context, not an assigned name for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Ipewik hill-valley corridor
correspondence.finding: The named Ipewik channel remains continuous through the southwestward hill-valley bends and small branching reaches. Several selected straight sections run north or west of mapped meanders. The geographic association uses the full connected river corridor and its successive tributary mouths, without inventing direct cross-hill channels along the coarse line.

correspondence.component_scope: Ipewik–Kukpuk junction and western Kukpuk reach
correspondence.finding: Near the Kayaksik Mountain setting, the Ipewik River is mapped joining Kukpuk River, which approaches from the south. The combined channel turns northwest and west across the coastal wetland plain. Repeated Kukpuk River labels and the continuous mapped channel establish the receiving-river identity. Local ponds and the Ogsochuk-area side-creek setting do not require a selected through-lake transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Coastal plain, delta branches and actual Marryat Inlet terminal
correspondence.finding: Kukpuk River continues across the wetland plain, around the coastal bends and into its broad branched delta at Marryat Inlet. The source explicitly labels the northern main mouth Kukpuk River and the receiving inlet Marryat Inlet; a southern distributary is separately labelled. The actual selected terminal is in this mapped mouth/inlet setting. No exact present shoreline, marsh-island edge, tidal opening, active distributary or seaward extension is assigned. Nearby coastal lakes are distinct mapped waterbodies outside the selected through-route.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Burnt Canyon opening and upper San Gorgonio canyon
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is on a mapped headward channel in the Burnt Canyon setting. The channel continues into the directly labelled San Gorgonio River through the Big Oaks/Gilman canyon setting and south through Banning Canyon. The selected start is not asserted to be the official or ultimate river source.

correspondence.component_scope: Banning–Cabazon pass and upper named river joins
correspondence.finding: Repeated San Gorgonio River labels and the connected wash corridor cover the eastward pass below Banning and Cabazon, including the Hathaway and Smith Creek joining settings and the approach toward Windy Point. Dashed channel and broad wash depiction do not establish perennial flow. The nearby Colorado River Aqueduct is separately shown; it is not treated as the selected through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: San Gorgonio–Whitewater joining setting and selected southwestern basin/plain excursion
correspondence.finding: The original cartography maps the San Gorgonio River joining Whitewater River by Windy Point and shows the Whitewater channel continuing east, then southeast. The selected route instead makes a substantial southwestern excursion across a rectangular-basin array and the Chino-side road/plain landscape before returning toward the river corridor. The inspected maps do not establish that selected through-connection. Nearby river naming, basin structures and modeled connectivity are not evidence of a surface-water transfer across it. This is broader than a minor bank or bend offset.

correspondence.component_scope: Palm Springs–Cathedral City–Rancho Mirage–Palm Desert corridor
correspondence.finding: Repeated Whitewater River labels and the connected mapped corridor support the long southeastward and then eastward valley reach, including the Palm Canyon Wash joining setting and the Cathedral City, Rancho Mirage and Palm Desert reaches. Numerous nearby ornamental ponds and side washes are distinct; no selected passage through each pond is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Indian Wells bend, Indio, Coachella and Thermal lower corridor
correspondence.finding: The cartography directly labels Whitewater River through Indian Wells, the northward Indio bend, Coachella and Thermal, continuing along a visibly straightened lower corridor. Wasteway Number Three and Wasteway Number Two are separately named side connections. Coachella Canal remains a distinct mapped canal, and its name is not transferred to the selected river. Facility operations, present discharge and any formal alternative lower-channel name were not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower road/pond approach and selected lake-entry transfer
correspondence.finding: The maps clearly show the lower Whitewater channel entering Salton Sea. The selected approach leaves the mapped channel toward the west, traverses road/pond terrain and the western lakeshore margin, then reaches the lake by a different selected line. No continuous mapped waterway establishes that full selected cross-terrain connection. This is not a claim about an exact current river-mouth vertex or the present waterline. The supported river-to-lake context cannot by itself supply the missing selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Long Salton Sea interior continuation and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The remaining selected southeastward continuation and its actual endpoint lie within the mapped Salton Sea waterbody. The lake is directly labelled in the original cartography. The long interior model line is not a mapped river channel and is not assigned the Whitewater River or San Gorgonio River name. No hydraulic path within the lake or exact present shoreline is asserted.
